articles.resume: Germany November unemployment change 9k vs 4k expected Prior 4k Germany November unemployment rate 6.4% vs 6.4% expected Prior 6.4% The number of people out of work in Germany rose by more than expected in November, though the jobless rate is seen holding steady on the month at 6.4%. Overall, the total number of unemployed persons rose to 3.025 million in seasonally adjusted terms. But when looking at the unadjusted total, it fell by 19,000 to 2.936 million in November with the labour office noting that the decline reflected the end of the autumn seasonal pickup. articles.resume: Spain November preliminary CPI +4.1% vs +4.6% y/y expected Prior +4.9% Spain November preliminary HICP +4.1% vs +4.7% y/y expected Prior +4.9% Much like the French report earlier, Spain's inflation numbers are also seen cooling off in November. articles.titre: France Q3 GDP revised lower as economic woes deepen
articles.resume: France Q3 final GDP -0.2% vs -0.1% q/q prelim Prior 0.0% Ouch. France was already the troubling spot in the euro area and the negative revision to the preliminary GDP estimates only continues to underscore that notion. In volume terms, the French economy contracted by 0.2% in Q3 following some tentative stability in the previous quarter. Domestic demand was pretty much subdued, stagnating on the quarter, while inventory changes contributed to 0.3% to quarterly GDP with net foreign trade being the main drag with a negative contribution of 0.6% on the quarter. Overall, the French economy is seen growing by just 0.1% so far this year and that is hardly encouraging for Europe's second-largest ec

articles.resume: France November preliminary CPI +2.9% vs +3.2% y/y expected Prior +3.4% France November preliminary HICP +3.2% vs +3.6% y/y expected Prior +3.7% Well, that's some good news for the French economy as inflation pressures are seen cooling back a little in November. The drop here is even below analyst estimates, with headline annual inflation dropping back below 3%. The monthly reading also shows that French inflation should ease by 0.7% in November, after having risen by 0.4% in October. Looking at the details, energy inflation falling off is a key factor driving that development. Of note, energy prices are seen rising by 19.2% in November compared to the 24.1% increase in October. articles.titre: US reportedly urged Venezuela, Iraq to consider quitting OPEC earlier this year
articles.resume: US president Trump has never been much of a fan of OPEC. And as it would seem, he'd quite like a few of its members to feel the same way. Washington reportedly even blocked Venezuela's annual membership payment, while Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman intervened over the summer to persuade the US to back off. articles.titre: China's industrial profits jump 20.1% in October as electronics do the heavy lifting
articles.resume: The data offers some support for Chinese and wider Asian technology supply-chain stocks, where profits are clearly strongest. Its value as a signal for the broader economy is limited, though, because consumer-facing sectors are still struggling. For commodities, stronger factory earnings are mildly supportive for industrial metals, but persistent property weakness caps the upside for steel-linked inputs such as iron ore. The yuan and China-sensitive currencies such as the Australian dollar are likely to take more direction from tariff headlines than from this release. Any new US or EU trade restrictions would hit the export-dependent firms that drove October's gains. --- Data post here: Chin

articles.titre: China's industrial profits growth speeds up to 20.1% y/y in October
articles.resume: China industrial profits, October Year-to-date: 16.0% y/y prior (jany - September) 15.5% October alone: 20.1% y/y prior 14.4% Profit growth at China's industrial firms accelerated sharply in October, with the single-month gain picking up to 20.1% from 14.4% in September. That lifted growth for the first ten months of the year to 16.0% from 15.5%. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.titre: Kiwi edges higher as official NZ election count confirms a hung parliament
articles.resume: The muted reaction suggests NZD traders are pricing politics as noise unless talks break down. The tail risk is a failed negotiation and a fresh election, which would bring a longer period of uncertainty and could weigh on the currency and New Zealand government bonds. Coalition deals that come with large fiscal commitments are the other thing to watch, especially for bond yields. Outside Wellington, the kiwi remains tied to global risk sentiment and the US dollar. The survey's market impact is usually small, though, and moves in global risk appetite and the US dollar are likely to matter more for the currency. articles.titre: Global electricity generation more than doubled from 2000 to 2025
articles.resume: The world generated 31.8 trillion kilowatthours (kWh) of electricity in 2025, more than double the 15.1 trillion kWh generated in 2000, according to our recently updated International Energy Statistics data. This growth in global electricity generation is driven by increasing electricity demand from global population and economic growth, and an increase in global median household income.

articles.titre: Category 2 Hurricane Isaias nears landfall, leading to production shut-ins
articles.resume: As of 4:00 a.m. central time on October 9, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration expects Hurricane Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, creating the potential for significant disruptions to energy infrastructure. Hurricane Isaias is the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season and will be the largest storm system to make landfall in the region since Hurricane Helene in September 2024.
